before:
The evidence supports a strong but deliberately scoped conclusion about the two production areas examined. TakeoffHandling proved highly amenable to isolated unit-level structural testing because its public interface allows legitimate state transitions, timing configuration, and ramp outputs to be controlled without modifying production code. Five focused tests exercised the normal takeoff lifecycle, landing/re-entry behavior, the skip-takeoff override, disarm reset, ramp thresholds, and minimum-gain behavior. The resulting 95.2% executable-line and 96.7% branch coverage is considered practically complete for the public production behavior. The residual default switch arm represents an invalid internal enum state and was not forced solely to increase the percentage.

The Failsafe study provides broader safety-policy evidence. The final twelve-test functional suite exercised the real Failsafe implementation through its framework path and raised coverage of the selected checkStateAndMode() scope from 81.9% to 100% for executable lines and from 49.1% to 85.3% for branches. The five-case MC/DC design demonstrated independent effect for all four atomic conditions in the selected mission-control-loss decision. One important oracle limitation was retained rather than hidden: changing condition C can make the selected compound decision false while the ordinary GCS-loss path still produces RTL. Structural branch evidence is therefore necessary to establish that independence pair.

The remaining Failsafe branch gaps were investigated individually. They consist of equivalent external-mode predicates and compiler/instrumentation exception edges rather than uncovered executable statements. The final 149/149 regression result further shows that the student test integration did not introduce observed regressions in the existing PX4 test suite. These results increase confidence in the tested Takeoff and Failsafe behaviors, but they do not justify a claim that PX4 as a whole is defect-free or comprehensively verified. Untested modules, hardware-dependent behavior, SITL/HIL interactions, concurrency, and environment-specific failures remain outside the scope of this assignment.
